# Purpose

The sample size is fixed at $N = 500$ (167 control, 167 harm message, 166 purity message).
This document is an *a priori* sensitivity analysis for the hypotheses in the Design table
(Table 1). For each type of test it estimates the probability that the test ends as
**supported**, **not supported** or **inconclusive** across a range of true effect sizes, with
the smallest effect size of interest (SESOI) as the reference point. The values marked
"[from Rmd]" in the Design table are collected in Section 10.

* SESOI: $d = 0.20$ for continuous outcomes; 0.36 on the log-odds scale for plant-based choice;
  0.20 SD of the outcome per SD of the moral value for each interaction.
* All continuous variables are standardized before analysis, so effects are in SD units.
* Every directional hypothesis is evaluated with two one-sided tests at $\alpha = .05$, with no
  correction for multiple testing:
    * **Supported**: the effect is greater than zero (one-sided $p < .05$; for indirect effects, the
      lower bound of the 90% CI is above zero).
    * **Not supported**: the effect is smaller than the SESOI (one-sided inferiority test,
      $p < .05$; for indirect effects, the upper bound of the 90% CI is below the SESOI).
    * **Inconclusive**: neither.
* H16 is tested in the positive direction only.

Hypotheses that use the same type of test are simulated once:

| Section | Simulated test | Hypotheses |
|---|---|---|
| 3 | Message effect, OLS | H1--H6, H17, H18 |
| 4 | Message effect, mixed logistic regression | H7, H8 |
| 5 | Moderation model for moralization: compound matching contrast $L$, single interaction, $b_8 - b_6$ | H9, H10, H11, H12 |
| 6 | Compound matching contrast, mixed logistic regression | H13 |
| 7 | Indirect effect in parallel mediation | H14, H15 |
| 8 | Serial indirect effect | H16 |
| 9 | Emotion crossover interaction | H19 |

Hypotheses that share a test have the same sampling distribution (e.g., $b_6$ and $b_8$, or the
two indirect effects of the parallel mediation model), so one simulation gives the power for all.

# Settings and helper functions

All assumptions are set here and can be changed before knitting.

```{r settings}
# Design
n_group  <- c(control = 167, harm = 167, purity = 166)   # N = 500
N        <- sum(n_group)
n_pairs  <- 12                                           # product-choice trials

# Inference
alpha    <- .05           # one-sided
sesoi_d  <- 0.20          # SD units
sesoi_lo <- 0.36          # log-odds (= 0.20 * pi / sqrt(3))
sesoi_ab <- 0.20^2        # two-path indirect effect (H14, H15)

# Effect-size grids
grid_d  <- c(0, 0.10, 0.20, 0.30, 0.40)
grid_lo <- c(0, 0.18, 0.36, 0.54, 0.72)

# Number of simulated data sets per grid value
n_sims      <- 2000       # OLS-based tests
n_sims_med  <- 1000       # mediation (Monte Carlo CIs)
n_sims_glmm <- 500        # mixed logistic models
n_mc        <- 5000       # Monte Carlo draws per mediation CI

# Plant-based choice model
p_plant        <- .50     # P(plant-based choice) in the control condition
sd_participant <- 1.5     # random-intercept SD, participants (log-odds)
sd_pair        <- 0.5     # random-intercept SD, product pairs (log-odds)

# Correlations
r_values    <- .40        # care/harm values with purity values
r_mediators <- .40        # perceived harm with perceived impurity (residual)
r_emotions  <- .40        # compassion with disgust (within person)

# Other true effects (held fixed)
main_msg_d  <- 0.20; main_val_d  <- 0.30   # moderation models, SD units
main_msg_lo <- 0.36; main_val_lo <- 0.36   # moderation models, log-odds
other_path  <- 0.30                        # parallel mediation: the other mediator's paths
path_m1_m2  <- 0.30                        # serial: perceived harm -> moralization
path_m2_y   <- 0.54                        # serial: moralization -> choice (log-odds per SD)

# Fixed design vectors
cond   <- rep(names(n_group), n_group)
harm   <- as.integer(cond == "harm")
purity <- as.integer(cond == "purity")
idx    <- rep(seq_len(N), each = n_pairs)           # long format for the choice data
pair   <- rep(seq_len(n_pairs), times = N)
```

```{r helpers}
z <- function(x) (x - mean(x)) / sd(x)

# Adds noise so the outcome has (about) unit variance, then standardizes it.
make_y <- function(lp) z(lp + rnorm(length(lp), 0, sqrt(1 - var(lp))))

# Two one-sided tests: supported (est > 0) and not supported (est < sesoi).
decide <- function(est, se, sesoi, df = Inf) {
  est <- unname(est)
  se  <- unname(se)
  sup <- unname(pt(est / se, df, lower.tail = FALSE) < alpha)
  inf <- unname(pt((est - sesoi) / se, df) < alpha)
  c(supported = sup, not_supported = !sup && inf)
}

# Same rules for an indirect effect (product of paths), using a 90% Monte Carlo CI.
decide_mc <- function(est, se, sesoi) {
  draws <- Reduce(`*`, Map(function(m, s) rnorm(n_mc, m, s), est, se))
  q <- unname(quantile(draws, c(.05, .95)))
  c(supported = q[1] > 0, not_supported = q[1] <= 0 && q[2] < sesoi)
}

# Moral values: two correlated, standardized scores.
make_values <- function(r = r_values) {
  V <- mvrnorm(N, c(0, 0), matrix(c(1, r, r, 1), 2))
  data.frame(care = z(V[, 1]), pur = z(V[, 2]))
}

# Simulated plant-based choices (long format) for a person-level linear predictor lp.
make_choices <- function(lp) {
  eta <- lp[idx] + rnorm(N, 0, sd_participant)[idx] + rnorm(n_pairs, 0, sd_pair)[pair]
  rbinom(N * n_pairs, 1, plogis(eta))
}

fit_glmm <- function(formula, dat)
  glmer(formula, data = dat, family = binomial, nAGQ = 0,
        control = glmerControl(calc.derivs = FALSE))

# Estimate and SE of a linear combination of coefficients (weights w, named).
contrast <- function(b, S, w) {
  wf <- setNames(rep(0, length(b)), names(b)); wf[names(w)] <- w
  c(est = sum(wf * b), se = sqrt(drop(t(wf) %*% S %*% wf)))
}

# Runs sim_fun n times for each row of grid and averages the results.
run_grid <- function(grid, sim_fun, n) {
  grid <- as.data.frame(grid)
  res <- t(sapply(seq_len(nrow(grid)), function(i)
    rowMeans(replicate(n, do.call(sim_fun, as.list(grid[i, , drop = FALSE]))))))
  cbind(grid, res)
}

# Outcome table for one test (prefix selects the test when a simulation returns several).
outcomes <- function(res, prefix = "") {
  sup <- res[[paste0(prefix, "supported")]]
  ns  <- res[[paste0(prefix, "not_supported")]]
  data.frame(res[, !grepl("supported", names(res)), drop = FALSE],
             Supported = sup, `Not supported` = ns, Inconclusive = 1 - sup - ns,
             check.names = FALSE)
}

# Effect size at which P(supported) reaches .80 (linear interpolation on the grid).
mde80 <- function(x, p) if (max(p) < .80) NA else approx(p, x, xout = .80, ties = mean)$y

show <- function(tab, caption) knitr::kable(tab, digits = 3, booktabs = TRUE,
                                            caption = caption, row.names = FALSE)

plot_outcomes <- function(tab, x, xlab, sesoi) {
  matplot(x, tab[, c("Supported", "Not supported", "Inconclusive")], type = "b",
          pch = 16, lty = 1, lwd = 2, col = c("darkgreen", "firebrick", "grey50"),
          ylim = c(0, 1), xlab = xlab, ylab = "Probability")
  abline(v = sesoi, lty = 3); abline(h = .80, lty = 3, col = "grey70")
  legend("right", c("Supported", "Not supported", "Inconclusive"), lwd = 2, bty = "n",
         col = c("darkgreen", "firebrick", "grey50"), cex = .8)
}
```

# Message effects on continuous outcomes (H1--H6, H17, H18)

Model: $y = b_0 + b_1\,\text{Harm} + b_2\,\text{Purity}$, with $y$ standardized (moralization,
perceived harm to animals, perceived impurity, compassion or disgust). The true effect $d$ is
placed on one message; the result is the same for $b_1$ and $b_2$.

```{r sim-message-ols}
set.seed(101)
sim_message_ols <- function(d) {
  y   <- make_y(d * harm)
  est <- summary(lm(y ~ harm + purity))$coefficients["harm", ]
  decide(est[1], est[2], sesoi_d, df = N - 3)
}
res_msg <- run_grid(data.frame(d = grid_d), sim_message_ols, n_sims)
tab_msg <- outcomes(res_msg)
show(tab_msg, "Message effect on a continuous outcome (H1--H6, H17, H18).")
plot_outcomes(tab_msg, grid_d, "True message effect (d)", sesoi_d)
```

# Message effects on plant-based choice (H7, H8)

Model: $\text{logit}(P) = b_0 + b_1\,\text{Harm} + b_2\,\text{Purity} + u_\text{participant} + u_\text{pair}$,
fitted with `glmer` (`nAGQ = 0`) to the 12 choices of each participant.

```{r sim-message-glmm}
set.seed(102)
sim_message_glmm <- function(b) {
  dat <- data.frame(choice = make_choices(qlogis(p_plant) + b * harm),
                    harm = harm[idx], purity = purity[idx],
                    id = factor(idx), pair = factor(pair))
  fit <- fit_glmm(choice ~ harm + purity + (1 | id) + (1 | pair), dat)
  est <- summary(fit)$coefficients["harm", ]
  decide(est[1], est[2], sesoi_lo)
}
res_mglmm <- run_grid(data.frame(b = grid_lo), sim_message_glmm, n_sims_glmm)
tab_mglmm <- outcomes(res_mglmm)
show(tab_mglmm, "Message effect on plant-based choice, log-odds (H7, H8).")
plot_outcomes(tab_mglmm, grid_lo, "True message effect (log-odds)", sesoi_lo)
```

# Moderation by moral values, moralization (H9--H12)

Model: moralization $= b_0 + b_1\text{Harm} + b_2\text{Purity} + b_3\text{CareV} + b_4\text{PurityV}
+ b_5\text{Harm}\times\text{CareV} + b_6\text{Purity}\times\text{CareV} + b_7\text{Harm}\times\text{PurityV}
+ b_8\text{Purity}\times\text{PurityV}$.

Under MFT, each message works better among people who hold the matching value: $b_5 = b_8 = m$,
and the mismatching interactions are zero ($b_6 = b_7 = 0$). The simulation varies $m$ and
records three tests from the same model:

* **H9**: compound matching contrast $L = (b_5 - b_7) - (b_6 - b_8)$; here $L = 2m$, SESOI 0.40.
* **H10**: the matching interaction $b_8$ (SESOI 0.20). **H11** tests $b_6$, which has the same
  sampling distribution, so the $b_8$ results apply to it.
* **H12**: the contrast $b_8 - b_6$ (SESOI 0.20).

The last grid row shows matching for the purity message only ($b_8 = 0.20$, $b_5 = 0$, so
$L = 0.20$). In that row $b_8$ and $b_8 - b_6$ equal their SESOI, so it gives the power of H10
and H12.

```{r sim-moderation-ols}
set.seed(103)
w_L <- c("harm:care" = 1, "harm:pur" = -1, "purity:care" = -1, "purity:pur" = 1)
sim_moderation_ols <- function(m_harm, m_purity) {
  v   <- make_values()
  y   <- make_y(main_msg_d * (harm + purity) + main_val_d * (v$care + v$pur) +
                m_harm * harm * v$care + m_purity * purity * v$pur)
  fit <- lm(y ~ (harm + purity) * (care + pur), data = cbind(y, harm, purity, v))
  b <- coef(fit); S <- vcov(fit); df <- N - 9
  L  <- contrast(b, S, w_L)
  b8 <- contrast(b, S, c("purity:pur" = 1))
  dc <- contrast(b, S, c("purity:pur" = 1, "purity:care" = -1))
  c(H9  = decide(L[1],  L[2],  2 * sesoi_d, df),
    H10 = decide(b8[1], b8[2], sesoi_d, df),
    H12 = decide(dc[1], dc[2], sesoi_d, df))
}
grid_mod <- rbind(data.frame(m_harm = grid_d, m_purity = grid_d),
                  data.frame(m_harm = 0, m_purity = sesoi_d))
res_mod <- run_grid(grid_mod, sim_moderation_ols, n_sims)
sym      <- seq_along(grid_d)          # rows with m_harm = m_purity
pur_only <- nrow(grid_mod)             # purity-only row

tab_h9  <- outcomes(res_mod, "H9.")
tab_h10 <- outcomes(res_mod, "H10.")
tab_h12 <- outcomes(res_mod, "H12.")
show(tab_h9,  "Compound matching contrast, L = m_harm + m_purity (H9).")
show(tab_h10, "Single matching interaction b8; also applies to b6 (H10, H11).")
show(tab_h12, "Contrast b8 - b6 (H12).")
plot_outcomes(tab_h9[sym, ], grid_d, "True matching interaction per message (m; L = 2m)", sesoi_d)
```

**Sensitivity to the correlation between care/harm and purity values.** The correlation is
unknown, so H9 is repeated for $r = .20$, $.40$ and $.60$ at $m = 0$ and $m = 0.20$.

```{r sim-moderation-r}
set.seed(104)
res_r <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c(.20, .40, .60), function(r) {
  r_values <<- r
  cbind(r = r, run_grid(data.frame(m_harm = c(0, sesoi_d), m_purity = c(0, sesoi_d)),
                        sim_moderation_ols, n_sims))
}))
r_values <- .40
show(data.frame(r = res_r$r, m = res_r$m_harm, Supported = res_r$H9.supported,
                `Not supported` = res_r$H9.not_supported, check.names = FALSE),
     "Compound matching contrast (H9) by the correlation between the moral values.")
```

# Compound matching contrast, plant-based choice (H13)

Same fixed terms as in Section 5, in the mixed logistic model of Section 4. Each matching
interaction is $m$ on the log-odds scale (SESOI 0.36), so $L = 2m$ (SESOI 0.72).

```{r sim-moderation-glmm}
set.seed(105)
sim_moderation_glmm <- function(m) {
  v   <- make_values()
  lp  <- qlogis(p_plant) + main_msg_lo * (harm + purity) + main_val_lo * (v$care + v$pur) +
         m * harm * v$care + m * purity * v$pur
  dat <- data.frame(choice = make_choices(lp), harm = harm[idx], purity = purity[idx],
                    care = v$care[idx], pur = v$pur[idx], id = factor(idx), pair = factor(pair))
  fit <- fit_glmm(choice ~ (harm + purity) * (care + pur) + (1 | id) + (1 | pair), dat)
  L   <- contrast(fixef(fit), as.matrix(vcov(fit)), w_L)
  decide(L[1], L[2], 2 * sesoi_lo)
}
res_gmod <- run_grid(data.frame(m = grid_lo[1:4]), sim_moderation_glmm, n_sims_glmm)
tab_h13  <- outcomes(res_gmod)
show(tab_h13, "Compound matching contrast on plant-based choice, L = 2m in log-odds (H13).")
```

# Parallel mediation (H14, H15)

X = message (both dummies), M1 = perceived harm, M2 = perceived impurity, Y = moralization.
The simulated route is Purity $\to$ M2 $\to$ Y, with path $a$ (message $\to$ mediator) and
path $b$ (mediator $\to$ moralization, controlling for the other mediator). The other mediator's
paths are fixed at `r other_path`. H14 (impurity route) and H15 (harm route) have the same
structure, so one simulation covers both. SESOI = 0.04 ($= 0.20^2$).

```{r sim-parallel}
set.seed(106)
sim_parallel <- function(a, b) {
  E  <- mvrnorm(N, c(0, 0), matrix(c(1, r_mediators, r_mediators, 1), 2))
  M1 <- z(other_path * purity + E[, 1])
  M2 <- z(a * purity + E[, 2])
  Y  <- make_y(other_path * M1 + b * M2)
  fa <- summary(lm(M2 ~ harm + purity))$coefficients["purity", ]
  fb <- summary(lm(Y ~ harm + purity + M1 + M2))$coefficients["M2", ]
  decide_mc(c(fa[1], fb[1]), c(fa[2], fb[2]), sesoi_ab)
}
res_par <- run_grid(expand.grid(b = c(0, 0.10, 0.20, 0.30), a = c(0.20, 0.30, 0.50)),
                    sim_parallel, n_sims_med)
tab_par <- outcomes(res_par)
tab_par <- cbind(tab_par[, c("a", "b")], `a x b` = tab_par$a * tab_par$b, tab_par[, -(1:2)])
show(tab_par, "Indirect effect in the parallel mediation model (H14, H15).")
```

# Serial mediation (H16)

X = message, M1 = perceived harm, M2 = moralization, Y = proportion of plant-based choices (of 12,
generated from the choice model of Section 4). Path $a$ (purity message $\to$ perceived harm)
varies; perceived harm $\to$ moralization is fixed at `r path_m1_m2` SD and moralization $\to$
choice at `r path_m2_y` log-odds per SD. H16 is tested in the positive direction only.

```{r sim-serial}
set.seed(107)
sim_serial <- function(a) {
  M1  <- make_y(a * purity)
  M2  <- make_y(path_m1_m2 * M1)
  eta <- qlogis(p_plant) + path_m2_y * M2 + rnorm(N, 0, sd_participant)
  P   <- plogis(outer(eta, rnorm(n_pairs, 0, sd_pair), "+"))
  Y   <- z(rowMeans(matrix(rbinom(N * n_pairs, 1, P), N)))
  f1 <- summary(lm(M1 ~ harm + purity))$coefficients["purity", ]
  f2 <- summary(lm(M2 ~ harm + purity + M1))$coefficients["M1", ]
  f3 <- summary(lm(Y ~ harm + purity + M1 + M2))$coefficients["M2", ]
  decide_mc(c(f1[1], f2[1], f3[1]), c(f1[2], f2[2], f3[2]), sesoi_d^3)
}
res_ser <- run_grid(data.frame(a = grid_d), sim_serial, n_sims_med)
tab_h16 <- data.frame(a = res_ser$a, Supported = res_ser$supported,
                      Inconclusive = 1 - res_ser$supported)
show(tab_h16, "Serial indirect effect, positive direction only (H16).")
```

# Emotion crossover (H19)

Model (harm and purity conditions only, $n = 333$, two ratings per person):
rating $= b_0 + b_1\text{Harm} + b_2\text{Compassion} + b_3\text{Harm}\times\text{Compassion}
+ u_\text{participant}$. With two ratings per person and a random intercept, the estimate and the
test of $b_3$ are the same as an OLS regression of the difference score (compassion $-$ disgust)
on Harm, which is used here for speed.

```{r sim-crossover}
set.seed(108)
keep <- cond != "control"
h    <- harm[keep]
sim_crossover <- function(b3) {
  E    <- mvrnorm(sum(keep), c(0, 0), matrix(c(1, r_emotions, r_emotions, 1), 2))
  comp <- z(b3 * h + E[, 1])
  disg <- z(E[, 2])
  est  <- summary(lm(I(comp - disg) ~ h))$coefficients["h", ]
  decide(est[1], est[2], sesoi_d, df = sum(keep) - 2)
}
res_cross <- run_grid(data.frame(b3 = grid_d), sim_crossover, n_sims)
tab_h19 <- outcomes(res_cross)
show(tab_h19, "Emotion crossover interaction (H19).")
plot_outcomes(tab_h19, grid_d, "True crossover interaction (SD)", sesoi_d)
```

# Values for the Design table

These values replace "[from Rmd]" in the Design table. *Power* is P(supported) at the SESOI.
*P(not supported given 0)* is the probability of concluding that the effect is smaller than the
SESOI when the true effect is zero. *Effect for .80 power* is the true effect at which
P(supported) reaches .80, interpolated on the grid (NA = not reached within the grid).

```{r design-table-values}
row <- function(hyps, sesoi, tab, x) {
  at <- which(abs(x - sesoi) < 1e-9); nul <- which(x == 0)
  ns <- if ("Not supported" %in% names(tab)) tab[["Not supported"]][nul] else NA
  data.frame(Hypotheses = hyps, SESOI = sesoi, Power = tab$Supported[at],
             `P(not supported given 0)` = ns,
             `Effect for .80 power` = mde80(x, tab$Supported), check.names = FALSE)
}
fixed_row <- function(hyps, sesoi, power, ns)
  data.frame(Hypotheses = hyps, SESOI = sesoi, Power = power,
             `P(not supported given 0)` = ns, `Effect for .80 power` = NA,
             check.names = FALSE)
par_at  <- which(tab_par$a == 0.20 & tab_par$b == 0.20)
par_nul <- which(tab_par$a == 0.20 & tab_par$b == 0)

values <- rbind(
  row("H1-H6, H17, H18", sesoi_d,      tab_msg,       grid_d),
  row("H7, H8",          sesoi_lo,     tab_mglmm,     grid_lo),
  row("H9 (scale of L)", 2 * sesoi_d,  tab_h9[sym, ], 2 * grid_d),
  fixed_row("H9, matching for one message only (L = 0.20)", 0.20,
            tab_h9$Supported[pur_only], NA),
  fixed_row("H10, H11", sesoi_d, tab_h10$Supported[pur_only], tab_h10[["Not supported"]][1]),
  fixed_row("H12",      sesoi_d, tab_h12$Supported[pur_only], tab_h12[["Not supported"]][1]),
  row("H13 (scale of L)", 2 * sesoi_lo, tab_h13,      2 * grid_lo[1:4]),
  fixed_row("H14, H15 (a = b = 0.20; null: a = 0.20, b = 0)", sesoi_ab,
            tab_par$Supported[par_at], tab_par[["Not supported"]][par_nul]),
  row("H16 (path a)",    sesoi_d,      tab_h16,       grid_d),
  row("H19",             sesoi_d,      tab_h19,       grid_d))
show(values, "Values for the Design table.")
```

# Assumptions

* Normal residuals for continuous outcomes; outcomes generated with unit variance and standardized.
* Plant-based choice: P(plant) = `r p_plant` in control; random-intercept SDs `r sd_participant`
  (participants) and `r sd_pair` (product pairs) on the log-odds scale; 12 choices per participant.
  Mixed models fitted with `nAGQ = 0`, a fast approximation to the default Laplace fit.
* Moderation models: message main effects `r main_msg_d` SD (`r main_msg_lo` log-odds), value
  main effects `r main_val_d` SD (`r main_val_lo` log-odds); correlation between the moral values
  `r r_values`.
* Mediation: 90% Monte Carlo CIs (`r n_mc` draws) in place of the percentile bootstrap; residual
  correlation between the mediators `r r_mediators`; fixed paths as stated in Sections 7 and 8.
* Emotions: within-person correlation between compassion and disgust `r r_emotions`.
* Simulations per grid value: `r n_sims` (OLS), `r n_sims_med` (mediation), `r n_sims_glmm`
  (mixed logistic). With 500 data sets the Monte Carlo SE of a probability is at most .022.

```{r session-info, cache = FALSE}
sessionInfo()
```
